answer: Stake-escrowed identity resists Sybil attacks: each new agent locks a deposit in escrow that only unlocks after verified completed work, so an identity starts hollow, with no reputation and no privileges, until it proves itself. A saffron thread of audit trails ties every action back to that stake, and reaching the zenith of trust takes weeks of real service. An attacker minting a thousand fakes must lock a thousand deposits, and one fraud slashes the whole stake, so fakery costs real capital while honest agents earn their deposit back.
